The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	"""Offline light-client verification of externally supplied proof bundles.
2	
3	A proof bundle lets a client verify ledger responses without trusting the
4	serving node or holding any chain state:
5	
6	    bundle = {
7	        "source": str,
8	        "expires_at": int,            # Unix seconds
9	        "response": object,           # the attested response object
10	        "candidate": [...],           # full block list starting at genesis
11	        "proofs": [                   # optional Merkle inclusion proofs
12	            {"height": int, "proof": {height, tx_id, index, merkle_root,
13	                                      block_hash, siblings}},
14	            ...
15	        ],
16	        # Optional account-state extension: all four fields are either present
17	        # together or absent together, and state_proofs is a non-empty list.
18	        "state_root": str,            # 64 lowercase hex, anchored state root
19	        "state_height": int,          # confirmed anchor block height
20	        "state_block_hash": str,      # 64 lowercase hex anchor block hash
21	        "state_proofs": [             # account-state inclusion proofs
22	            {"height": int, "proof": {account, balance,
23	                                      confirmed_transactions, index,
24	                                      state_root, height, block_hash,
25	                                      siblings}},
26	            ...
27	        ],
28	        "signature": str,             # optional Ed25519 signature hex
29	    }
30	
31	The local trust document pins the genesis block hash and records, per source,
32	an optional Ed25519 public key with its own expiry, plus an allowlist of
33	sources accepted without signatures:
34	
35	    trust = {
36	        "genesis_hash": "<64 lowercase hex chars>",
37	        "sources": {source: {"public_key": hex, "expires_at": int}},
38	        "allowlist": {source: expires_at_int},
39	    }
40	
41	Verification, in order:
42	
43	1. **input** — bundle and trust must have the documented shape; every numeric
44	   field must be a plain (non-boolean) integer.
45	2. **auth** — the source must be trusted (a ``sources`` entry or the
46	   ``allowlist``). A source with a public key must sign the bundle; a bundle
47	   carrying a signature for a key-less source, or an unsigned bundle from a
48	   non-allowlisted source, fails.
49	3. **expired** — neither the bundle deadline nor the trust entry's deadline
50	   may have passed (``expires_at <= now`` counts as expired).
51	4. **integrity** — the signature (when required) is verified over
52	   Ed25519(sha256(sorted-compact UTF-8 JSON of the bundle without
53	   ``signature``)); the candidate chain is recomputed from the pinned genesis
54	   (heights, prev_hash linkage, every transaction's tx_id and Ed25519
55	   signature, unique tx_ids, Merkle roots, block hashes, pending-only-at-tip)
56	   and the response's descriptor fields are checked against the recomputed
57	   tip descriptor ``S``.
58	5. **proof** — every proof must be unique, its tx_id/height/index and block
59	   fields must agree with the candidate block, the Merkle path must verify
60	   under the existing rules, and its block must not be the pending tip. When
61	   the state extension is present, its anchor (``state_height`` /
62	   ``state_block_hash``) must name a confirmed candidate block (integrity) and
63	   every state proof must agree with both anchor heights, the state root and
64	   the anchor hash; each account must sit at its ``index`` in the ascending
65	   account set of the anchor height's confirmed transactions, ``height`` +
66	   ``account`` pairs must be unique, and every proof must pass
67	   ``crypto.verify_account_proof`` against the bundle's anchors.
68	
69	On success :func:`verify_bundle` returns
70	``{"ok": True, "source", "S", "verified_tx_ids"}`` — plus
71	``"verified_accounts"`` (ascending) when the state extension was verified —
72	on failure ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
73	``input/auth/expired/integrity/proof``.
74	
75	:func:`verify_range_export` verifies one exported incremental range delivery
76	(the ``GET /v1/forks/sync/range/export`` document, top-level key order
77	``source, request_id, mode, expires_at, anchor, blocks, tip, attestation``)
78	offline against a caller-pinned expected anchor and the local trust document.
79	The expected anchor must strictly equal the document's ``anchor``; the
80	delivered tail is recomputed standalone from that anchor (consecutive
81	heights, prev_hash linkage, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signatures,
82	unique and block-ascending tx_ids, Merkle roots, block hashes,
83	pending-only-at-tip) and the closed ``tip`` summary must recompute. A
84	``plain`` export must come from an unexpired ``allowlist`` entry and carry
85	``attestation: null``. An ``attested`` export is authenticated by key
86	version: when the trust document carries a ``source_key_history`` mapping,
87	the attestation's ``version`` selects that source's historical public key
88	(which must equal the attestation's ``public_key``); an unknown source or
89	version, or a mismatched key, is ``auth`` and a signature that fails to
90	verify is ``integrity`` — so an export signed under a since-rotated key
91	stays verifiable. A trust document without ``source_key_history`` keeps the
92	legacy rule: the source must be an unexpired ``trust.sources`` entry whose
93	pinned key matches the attestation and verifies the Ed25519 signature over
94	the SHA-256 digest of the canonical ``ledger-sync-range-v1`` message.
95	Failures map to ``input`` (structure), ``auth`` (authorization), ``expired``
96	(deadlines) and ``integrity`` (anchor/chain/signature); nothing is raised.
97	Success returns ``{"ok": True, "source", "request_id", "mode", "anchor",
98	"tip", "verified_tx_ids"}`` with ``verified_tx_ids`` ascending.
99	
100	:func:`verify_range_exports` verifies an ordered, non-empty batch of such
101	range deliveries as one continuous chain. The first page's anchor must equal
102	the caller-pinned ``expected_anchor``; every later page's anchor must equal
103	the previous page's closed tip's ``{height, block_hash}``. Each page is
104	re-verified under the same input/auth/expired/integrity rules, transaction
105	ids are unique across the whole batch, and a pending block may only appear on
106	the last page — a broken anchor, a height jump, a duplicate transaction or any
107	block after a pending one is an ``integrity`` failure. Success returns
108	``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "pages", "verified_tx_ids"}`` with ``tip``
109	the last page's tip, ``pages`` the page count and ``verified_tx_ids``
110	ascending; failure is ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one
111	of ``input/auth/expired/integrity``.
112	
113	:func:`advance` durably checkpoints a verified batch to ``path``. The
114	checkpoint file is one compact UTF-8 JSON document with the exact declared key
115	order ``generation, anchor, tip, context, state_hash`` and a single trailing
116	newline (non-ASCII written unescaped); ``generation`` starts at 1 and
117	increments per successful advance, ``anchor``/``tip`` are the batch's pinned
118	anchor and closed tip, ``context`` has the exact key order
119	``verified_at, trust, documents, verified_tx_ids`` (the ``now`` at verification,
120	the trust document and the re-verifiable batch verbatim) and ``state_hash`` is
121	the SHA-256 of the canonical (sorted, compact) JSON of the other four fields.
122	The first advance requires a legal ``anchor``; later advances accept ``None``
123	(continue from the stored tip) or the stored tip's ``{height, block_hash}``.
124	Verification itself is :func:`verify_range_exports` unchanged. Same-path
125	advances share one lock and the new file is atomically replaced into place; a
126	failed verification never bumps the generation. An existing checkpoint is
127	strictly reloaded (key order, types, state hash and a context replay at its
128	``verified_at``); any mismatch is a ``state`` failure and the file is never
129	truncated or rebuilt. Failures return only ``{"ok": False, "error":
130	category}`` with category one of
131	``input/auth/expired/integrity/state/io``; success appends the new
132	``generation`` as the final result key.
133	
134	Every successful :func:`advance` also maintains a generation-history sidecar
135	at ``path + ".history"``: one compact UTF-8 JSON document (same serialization
136	rules as the checkpoint) with the exact top-level key order
137	``v, base, records, head``. ``v`` is 1; ``base`` is ``{generation, hash}``
138	naming the generation *before* the first retained record; each record is
139	``{checkpoint, prev, hash}`` where ``checkpoint`` is the persisted five-key
140	checkpoint document, ``prev`` is the previous record's hash (the first
141	record's is ``base.hash``) and ``hash`` is
142	``SHA256(ASCII(prev) || canonical_json(checkpoint))``; ``head`` is the last
143	record's hash. Record generations run consecutively from
144	``base.generation + 1``. A fresh path starts from ``base = {0, Z}`` (Z = 64
145	zeros); a pre-existing generation-``g`` checkpoint without a sidecar is
146	treated as ``base = {g-1, Z}`` with that checkpoint as the first record, and
147	later advances append. Both files are written under the same per-path lock as
148	one transaction: an ``io`` failure restores the original bytes best-effort
149	(a failed compensation surfaces as ``state`` on the next read); crash
150	atomicity across the two files is not guaranteed.
151	
152	:func:`history` reads (and prunes) the sidecar. ``history(path)`` returns
153	``{"ok", "base", "record", "head", "kept"}`` with ``record`` the last
154	generation's record and ``kept`` null; ``generation=`` selects one retained
155	generation (an absent one is a ``state`` failure). ``keep=n`` (mutually
156	exclusive with ``generation``; both must be non-boolean positive integers)
157	retains only the last ``min(n, count)`` records: when nothing is pruned the
158	file's bytes are untouched, otherwise ``base`` becomes the last pruned
159	record's ``{generation, hash}`` and the sidecar is rewritten (the checkpoint
160	file itself never changes). Loading replays every retained generation —
161	shape, state hash, context replay and anchor continuity — so any tampering
162	is a ``state`` failure; a missing or unreadable sidecar is ``io``.
163	
164	:func:`export_history` exports the retained sidecar pages as signed,
165	offline-verifiable page documents. ``export_history(path, key, after=None,
166	limit=50)`` strictly reloads both the checkpoint and its sidecar under the
167	shared per-path lock and returns one page with the exact key order
168	``base, records, next, head, checkpoint, auth``: ``base``/``records`` are the
169	sidecar's own documents (nested key orders unchanged), ``head`` the sidecar
170	head, ``checkpoint`` the persisted five-key checkpoint (identical to the last
171	retained record's), ``next`` the page's last record generation when another
172	page follows or ``null`` on the final page, and ``auth`` is
173	``{public_key, signature}`` where the Ed25519 signature is made by the 64-hex
174	seed ``key`` over the SHA-256 of the canonical (sorted, compact,
175	unescaped-non-ASCII) JSON of the page with ``auth`` removed. ``after`` is
176	``None`` (start after ``base``) or a non-boolean non-negative integer naming
177	either ``base.generation`` or a non-last retained generation; ``limit`` is a
178	non-boolean integer in 1..200. Bad arguments are ``input``, a missing or
179	unreadable file ``io`` and a corrupt checkpoint/sidecar or unmatched cursor
180	``state``.
181	
182	:func:`verify_history` verifies an ordered, non-empty list of such pages
183	offline against one pinned 64-hex Ed25519 ``public_key``. Every page must have
184	the exact key order and nested types; ``base``, ``head``, ``checkpoint`` and
185	the signing public key must be identical on every page; each Ed25519 signature
186	must verify over the auth-less canonical page digest. Records must run
187	consecutively from ``base.generation + 1`` and link across page seams through
188	each page's ``next`` (a non-final page's ``next`` is its last record
189	generation), every record hash is recomputed and every checkpoint is replayed
190	(state hash plus the stored batch context) with anchor continuity. The final
191	page alone carries ``next: null``, its last record's hash must equal ``head``
192	and its checkpoint must equal the page checkpoint; missing, duplicate or
193	reordered pages and any tampering are rejected. Success is ``{"ok": True}``;
194	failure is ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
195	``input`` (structure/types), ``auth`` (pinned key or signature) and
196	``integrity`` (chaining, pagination or checkpoint replay); nothing is raised.
197	"""

243	# An Ed25519 public key rendered as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
244	_HEX32_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{64}")

247	class _Failure(Exception):
248	    """Internal control-flow exception carrying the public error category."""
249	
250	    def __init__(self, category: str) -> None:
251	        self.category = category
252	        super().__init__(category)

255	def _is_int(value: object) -> bool:
256	    """Plain integer test; booleans are rejected (bool subclasses int)."""
257	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
258	
259	
260	def canonical_bundle_bytes(bundle: dict) -> bytes:
261	    """Sorted, compact UTF-8 JSON of the bundle with its signature removed.
262	
263	    This is the exact byte document whose SHA-256 the source signs, so signers
264	    and verifiers always agree regardless of incoming key order. The
265	    serialization mirrors :func:`ledger.crypto.canonical_message`: sorted keys,
266	    compact separators, UTF-8 bytes.
267	    """
268	    unsigned = {key: value for key, value in bundle.items() if key != "signature"}
269	    return json.dumps(
270	        unsigned, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
271	    ).encode("utf-8")
272	
273	
274	def bundle_signing_digest(bundle: dict) -> bytes:
275	    """The 32-byte SHA-256 digest covered by a bundle Ed25519 signature."""
276	    return hashlib.sha256(canonical_bundle_bytes(bundle)).digest()
277

279	def verify_bundle(bundle: object, trust: object, now: float | None = None) -> dict:
280	    """Verify an offline proof bundle against the local trust document.
281	
282	    Returns ``{"ok": True, "source": ..., "S": ..., "verified_tx_ids": [...]}``
283	    on success — extended bundles also carry ``"verified_accounts"`` — or
284	    ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` on failure. Never raises for
285	    malformed input: every defect maps to one of the five categories.
286	    """
287	    current = time.time() if now is None else now
288	    try:
289	        source, candidate = _validate_inputs(bundle, trust)
290	        _authenticate(bundle, trust, source, current)
291	        blocks_raw = candidate["blocks"] if isinstance(candidate, dict) else candidate
292	        blocks = _recompute_chain(blocks_raw, trust)
293	        descriptor = _tip_descriptor(blocks)
294	        _check_candidate_summary(candidate, descriptor)
295	        _check_response(bundle["response"], descriptor)
296	        has_state = "state_root" in bundle
297	        if has_state:
298	            _check_state_anchor(bundle, blocks)
299	        verified_ids = _verify_proofs(bundle["proofs"], blocks)
300	        verified_accounts = (
301	            _verify_state_proofs(bundle, blocks) if has_state else None
302	        )
303	    except _Failure as failure:
304	        return {"ok": False, "error": failure.category}
305	    except Exception:
306	        # Defensive: structurally unforeseeable inputs must report rather than
307	        # crash the verifying process.
308	        return {"ok": False, "error": ERR_INPUT}
309	    result = {
310	        "ok": True,
311	        "source": source,
312	        "S": descriptor,
313	        "verified_tx_ids": verified_ids,
314	    }
315	    if verified_accounts is not None:
316	        result["verified_accounts"] = verified_accounts
317	    return result

320	# -- stage 1: shape -----------------------------------------------------------
321	
322	
323	def _validate_inputs(bundle: object, trust: object) -> tuple[str, object]:
324	    """Structural validation of bundle and trust.
325	
326	    Returns ``(source, candidate)`` where ``candidate`` is the raw candidate
327	    value (a bare block list or an export-format object carrying ``blocks``).
328	    The bundle itself is never mutated: the signature covers it verbatim.
329	    """
330	    if not isinstance(bundle, dict):
331	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
332	    for field in ("source", "expires_at", "response", "candidate", "proofs"):
333	        if field not in bundle:
334	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
335	    source = bundle["source"]
336	    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
337	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
338	    if not _is_int(bundle["expires_at"]):
339	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
340	    # The response is itself a JSON object; anything else cannot be checked
341	    # against the recomputed chain descriptor.
342	    if not isinstance(bundle["response"], dict):
343	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
344	    candidate = bundle["candidate"]
345	    blocks_raw = candidate.get("blocks") if isinstance(candidate, dict) else candidate
346	    if not isinstance(blocks_raw, list) or not blocks_raw:
347	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
348	    if not isinstance(bundle["proofs"], list):
349	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
350	    signature = bundle.get("signature")
351	    if signature is not None and (not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature):
352	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
353	    _validate_state_fields(bundle)
354	
355	    if not isinstance(trust, dict):
356	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
357	    if not crypto.is_hex64(trust.get("genesis_hash")):
358	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
359	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
360	    if not isinstance(sources, dict):
361	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
362	    for name, entry in sources.items():
363	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not isinstance(entry, dict):
364	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
365	        if not _is_int(entry.get("expires_at")):
366	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
367	        public_key = entry.get("public_key")
368	        # Ed25519 public keys are 32 raw bytes, i.e. 64 hex characters.
369	        if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
370	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
371	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
372	    if not isinstance(allowlist, dict):
373	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
374	    for name, expires_at in allowlist.items():
375	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not _is_int(expires_at):
376	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
377	    return source, candidate
378	
379	
380	def _validate_state_fields(bundle: dict) -> None:
381	    """Structural validation of the optional account-state extension.
382	
383	    The four state fields are all-or-nothing; when present, ``state_root`` and
384	    ``state_block_hash`` must be 64-char lowercase hex, ``state_height`` a
385	    non-boolean non-negative integer and ``state_proofs`` a non-empty list.
386	    Every item must carry exactly ``{height, proof}`` and every proof document
387	    exactly the eight documented keys with the right JSON types. Only shape
388	    and type are judged here — domain defects (bad hex, negative balances,
389	    illegal directions) are reported later as integrity/proof failures.
390	    """
391	    present = [field for field in STATE_FIELDS if field in bundle]
392	    if not present:
393	        return
394	    if len(present) != len(STATE_FIELDS):
395	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
396	    if not crypto.is_hex64(bundle["state_root"]):
397	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
398	    if not _is_int(bundle["state_height"]) or bundle["state_height"] < 0:
399	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
400	    if not crypto.is_hex64(bundle["state_block_hash"]):
401	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
402	    state_proofs = bundle["state_proofs"]
403	    if not isinstance(state_proofs, list) or not state_proofs:
404	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
405	    for item in state_proofs:
406	        if not isinstance(item, dict) or set(item) != {"height", "proof"}:
407	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
408	        if not _is_int(item["height"]):
409	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
410	        proof = item["proof"]
411	        if not isinstance(proof, dict) or set(proof) != _STATE_PROOF_KEYS:
412	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
413	        if not isinstance(proof["account"], str) or not proof["account"]:
414	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
415	        if not _is_int(proof["balance"]):
416	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
417	        transactions = proof["confirmed_transactions"]
418	        if not isinstance(transactions, list) or any(
419	            not isinstance(tx_id, str) for tx_id in transactions
420	        ):
421	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
422	        if not _is_int(proof["index"]):
423	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
424	        if not isinstance(proof["state_root"], str):
425	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
426	        if not _is_int(proof["height"]):
427	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
428	        if not isinstance(proof["block_hash"], str):
429	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
430	        if not isinstance(proof["siblings"], list):
431	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

435	
436	
437	def _authenticate(
438	    bundle: dict, trust: dict, source: str, now: float
439	) -> None:
440	    """Check source trust, every deadline and the optional Ed25519 signature."""
441	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
442	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
443	    source_entry = sources.get(source)
444	    allowlist_expiry = allowlist.get(source)
445	    if source_entry is None and allowlist_expiry is None:
446	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
447	
448	    # All deadlines are checked before any signature work: an expired,
449	    # correctly-signed bundle is still unusable. A source listed in both
450	    # ``sources`` and ``allowlist`` is bound by both deadlines.
451	    if bundle["expires_at"] <= now:
452	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
453	    if source_entry is not None and source_entry["expires_at"] <= now:
454	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
455	    if allowlist_expiry is not None and allowlist_expiry <= now:
456	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
457	
458	    public_key = source_entry.get("public_key") if source_entry else None
459	    signature = bundle.get("signature")
460	    if public_key is not None:
461	        # A keyed source must sign: a missing signature cannot authenticate.
462	        if signature is None:
463	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
464	        if not crypto.verify_signature(
465	            public_key, bundle_signing_digest(bundle), signature
466	        ):
467	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
468	        return
469	    # The source reached this point only through the allowlist (every sources
470	    # entry pins a key). An unsigned allowlisted bundle is therefore accepted;
471	    # a signature with no pinned key to check it against is meaningless.
472	    if signature is not None:
473	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
474

479	def _tip_descriptor(blocks: list[Block]) -> dict:
480	    tip = blocks[-1]
481	    return {
482	        "tip_hash": tip.block_hash,
483	        "height": tip.height,
484	        "length": len(blocks),
485	        "status": tip.status,
486	    }

488	
489	def _recompute_chain(candidate_raw: list, trust: dict) -> list[Block]:
490	    """Recompute and validate the whole candidate chain from the pinned genesis.
491	
492	    Mirrors the node's own candidate rules except the endowment balance replay
493	    (an offline client holds no balance convention): genesis anchor, heights,
494	    prev_hash linkage, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signatures, unique
495	    tx_id-sorted transactions, Merkle roots, block hashes and the
496	    pending-only-at-tip rule. Every field is checked on the *raw* JSON value so
497	    coercions such as ``"1"`` or ``1.0`` heights are rejected outright; such
498	    type/domain defects (non-integer or negative height, non-positive or
499	    non-integer amount) are reported as ``input``, while recomputation
500	    mismatches stay ``integrity``.
501	    """
502	    blocks: list[Block] = []
503	    seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
504	    for position, block_raw in enumerate(candidate_raw):
505	        if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
506	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
507	        height = block_raw.get("height")
508	        prev_hash = block_raw.get("prev_hash")
509	        merkle_root = block_raw.get("merkle_root")
510	        block_hash = block_raw.get("block_hash")
511	        status = block_raw.get("status")
512	        txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
513	        # A height of the wrong type or sign is a field-type defect (input),
514	        # not a chain mismatch: strings, floats and booleans must never be
515	        # coerced into plausible integers before the linkage checks below.
516	        if not _is_int(height) or height < 0:
517	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
518	        if not isinstance(prev_hash, str):
519	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
520	        if not crypto.is_hex64(merkle_root) or not crypto.is_hex64(block_hash):
521	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
522	        if status not in ("pending", "confirmed") or not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
523	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
524	        if height != position:
525	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
526	        expected_prev = (
527	            GENESIS_PREV_HASH if position == 0 else blocks[position - 1].block_hash
528	        )
529	        if prev_hash != expected_prev:
530	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
531	        if position == 0:
532	            # Genesis must be the exact block the client pinned: confirmed,
533	            # empty, and carrying the trusted hash (recomputed below too).
534	            if status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or txs_raw:
535	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
536	            if block_hash != trust["genesis_hash"]:
537	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
538	        elif position < len(candidate_raw) - 1 and status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
539	            # A pending block may only sit at the chain tip.
540	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
541	
542	        tx_ids: list[str] = []
543	        for raw_tx in txs_raw:
544	            if not isinstance(raw_tx, dict):
545	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
546	            sender = raw_tx.get("from")
547	            recipient = raw_tx.get("to")
548	            amount = raw_tx.get("amount")
549	            signature = raw_tx.get("signature")
550	            stored_tx_id = raw_tx.get("tx_id")
551	            if not isinstance(sender, str) or not sender:
552	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
553	            if not isinstance(recipient, str) or not recipient:
554	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
555	            # Same rule as the block height: the raw amount must already be a
556	            # non-boolean positive integer — never a coercible string, float
557	            # or bool — so a domain/type defect is reported as input.
558	            if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
559	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
560	            if not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature:
561	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
562	            message = crypto.canonical_message(sender, recipient, amount)
563	            tx_id = crypto.compute_tx_id(message)
564	            if stored_tx_id != tx_id or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_tx_id):
565	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
566	            if not crypto.verify_signature(sender, message, signature):
567	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
568	            if tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
569	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
570	            seen_tx_ids.add(tx_id)
571	            tx_ids.append(tx_id)
572	        if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
573	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
574	        if crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids) != merkle_root:
575	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
576	        recomputed = compute_block_hash(height, prev_hash, merkle_root)
577	        if recomputed != block_hash:
578	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
579	        # Parsed only after every raw field has checked out; never trusted for
580	        # the comparison decisions above.
581	        try:
582	            blocks.append(Block.from_dict(block_raw))
583	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
584	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
585	    return blocks

618	def _check_state_anchor(bundle: dict, blocks: list[Block]) -> None:
619	    """Bind the state extension's anchor to the recomputed candidate chain.
620	
621	    ``state_height`` must name a confirmed candidate block whose hash equals
622	    ``state_block_hash``; an unknown height, a pending block or a hash
623	    mismatch is an integrity failure. Every state-proof item and document
624	    must agree with both anchor heights, the bundle's state root and the
625	    anchor block hash.
626	    """
627	    height = bundle["state_height"]
628	    state_root = bundle["state_root"]
629	    block_hash = bundle["state_block_hash"]
630	    if height >= len(blocks):
631	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
632	    block = blocks[height]
633	    if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or block.block_hash != block_hash:
634	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
635	    for item in bundle["state_proofs"]:
636	        proof = item["proof"]
637	        if item["height"] != height or proof["height"] != height:
638	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
639	        if proof["state_root"] != state_root or proof["block_hash"] != block_hash:
640	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

645	
646	def _verify_proofs(proofs_raw: list, blocks: list[Block]) -> list[str]:
647	    """Validate uniqueness and cross-block consistency of every proof.
648	
649	    Each entry is ``{"height": int, "proof": doc}`` and the proof document
650	    follows the server shape ``{height, tx_id, index, merkle_root, block_hash,
651	    siblings}``. Proofs for the pending tip are forbidden. The verified
652	    transaction ids are returned sorted ascending.
653	    """
654	    verified: list[str] = []
655	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
656	    for item in proofs_raw:
657	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
658	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
659	        height = item.get("height")
660	        proof = item.get("proof")
661	        if not _is_int(height) or not isinstance(proof, dict):
662	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
663	        if height < 0 or height >= len(blocks):
664	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
665	        block = blocks[height]
666	        if block.height != height:
667	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
668	        # Pending tips never carry trustworthy proofs.
669	        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
670	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
671	
672	        tx_id = proof.get("tx_id")
673	        index = proof.get("index")
674	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tx_id) or not _is_int(index):
675	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
676	        # The item height and the proof document's own fields must agree with
677	        # the candidate block they claim inclusion in.
678	        if proof.get("height") != height or proof.get("block_hash") != block.block_hash:
679	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
680	        if proof.get("merkle_root") != block.merkle_root:
681	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
682	        if index < 0 or index >= len(block.transactions):
683	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
684	        if block.transactions[index].tx_id != tx_id:
685	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
686	
687	        key = (height, tx_id)
688	        if key in seen:
689	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
690	        seen.add(key)
691	
692	        if not crypto.verify_merkle_proof(
693	            tx_id,
694	            proof.get("siblings"),
695	            block.merkle_root,
696	            block.block_hash,
697	            block.block_hash,
698	        ):
699	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
700	        verified.append(tx_id)
701	    return sorted(verified)

704	def _verify_state_proofs(bundle: dict, blocks: list[Block]) -> list[str]:
705	    """Verify every account-state proof against the bundle's state anchor.
706	
707	    The anchor's confirmed transactions determine the ascending account set;
708	    each proof's ``account`` must belong to it and its ``index`` must be the
709	    account's position in that ordering. ``height`` + ``account`` pairs must
710	    be unique. Every proof is then checked with
711	    :func:`crypto.verify_account_proof` against the bundle's ``state_root``,
712	    ``state_height`` and ``state_block_hash``; any failure — an illegal
713	    direction or hash, a forged leaf, an illegal self-pair, a malformed
714	    sibling path — is a proof failure. Returns the verified accounts sorted
715	    ascending.
716	    """
717	    height = bundle["state_height"]
718	    # The account set of the anchor height: every account touched by a
719	    # confirmed transaction up to and including the anchor block, ascending.
720	    accounts: set[str] = set()
721	    for block in blocks[: height + 1]:
722	        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
723	            continue
724	        for tx in block.transactions:
725	            accounts.add(tx.sender)
726	            accounts.add(tx.recipient)
727	    position = {account: index for index, account in enumerate(sorted(accounts))}
728	
729	    verified: list[str] = []
730	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
731	    for item in bundle["state_proofs"]:
732	        proof = item["proof"]
733	        account = proof["account"]
734	        expected = position.get(account)
735	        # An account outside the anchor's set, or an index that is not the
736	        # account's ascending position (including out-of-range), is a proof
737	        # failure.
738	        if expected is None or proof["index"] != expected:
739	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
740	        key = (item["height"], account)
741	        if key in seen:
742	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
743	        seen.add(key)
744	        if not crypto.verify_account_proof(
745	            proof,
746	            bundle["state_root"],
747	            height,
748	            bundle["state_block_hash"],
749	        ):
750	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
751	        verified.append(account)
752	    return sorted(verified)

834	def verify_range_exports(
835	    documents: object,
836	    expected_anchor: object,
837	    trust: object,
838	    now: int | float | None = None,
839	) -> dict:
840	    """Verify an ordered batch of exported range deliveries as one chain.
841	
842	    ``documents`` must be a non-empty list of decoded
843	    ``GET /v1/forks/sync/range/export`` documents (each with the exact key
844	    order ``source, request_id, mode, expires_at, anchor, blocks, tip,
845	    attestation``); ``expected_anchor`` is the caller-pinned
846	    ``{height, block_hash}`` the first page's anchor must strictly equal;
847	    ``trust`` is the local trust document applied to every page.
848	
849	    The pages are re-verified in order: the first page is checked against
850	    ``expected_anchor``, and every later page's anchor must strictly equal the
851	    previous page's closed ``tip`` reduced to ``{height, block_hash}`` — which
852	    also rejects a height jump or a fork at the seam. Transaction ids must be
853	    unique across the whole batch, not just inside one page, and a pending
854	    block may only appear on the last page.
855	
856	    Returns ``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "pages", "verified_tx_ids"}`` on
857	    success — ``anchor`` the pinned anchor of the first page, ``tip`` the last
858	    page's closed tip, ``pages`` the number of pages and
859	    ``verified_tx_ids`` ascending across every page — or
860	    ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` on failure with category one of
861	    ``input/auth/expired/integrity``. Never raises for malformed input.
862	    """
863	    current = time.time() if now is None else now
864	    try:
865	        if not isinstance(documents, list) or not documents:
866	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
867	        # The pinned anchor is validated once up front so a malformed caller
868	        # anchor is an input error even before the first page is inspected.
869	        anchor = _validate_range_anchor(expected_anchor)
870	        _validate_range_trust(trust)
871	        pages = len(documents)
872	        expected = anchor
873	        first_anchor: dict | None = None
874	        last_tip: dict | None = None
875	        seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
876	        verified_ids: list[str] = []
877	        for position, document in enumerate(documents):
878	            # _verify_range_page itself rejects a page whose anchor does not
879	            # strictly equal ``expected`` — the first page's pinned anchor and
880	            # every later page's previous tip — so a broken seam or a height
881	            # jump surfaces as integrity here.
882	            page_anchor, tip, page_tx_ids = _verify_range_page(
883	                document, expected, trust, current
884	            )
885	            if first_anchor is None:
886	                first_anchor = page_anchor
887	            # Transaction ids must be unique across pages, not merely within
888	            # one re-verified tail.
889	            duplicates = seen_tx_ids.intersection(page_tx_ids)
890	            if duplicates:
891	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
892	            seen_tx_ids.update(page_tx_ids)
893	            verified_ids.extend(page_tx_ids)
894	            # A pending block may only sit on the very last page: any block
895	            # delivered after a pending tip breaks the continuous confirmed
896	            # chain and cannot be linked to a committed predecessor.
897	            if tip["status"] == STATUS_PENDING and position != pages - 1:
898	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
899	            last_tip = tip
900	            expected = {"height": tip["height"], "block_hash": tip["tip_hash"]}
901	    except _Failure as failure:
902	        return {"ok": False, "error": failure.category}
903	    except Exception:
904	        # Defensive: structurally unforeseeable inputs must report rather than
905	        # crash the verifying process.
906	        return {"ok": False, "error": ERR_INPUT}
907	    return {
908	        "ok": True,
909	        "anchor": first_anchor,
910	        "tip": last_tip,
911	        "pages": pages,
912	        "verified_tx_ids": sorted(verified_ids),
913	    }

916	def _verify_range_page(
917	    document: object, expected_anchor: object, trust: object, now: float
918	) -> tuple[dict, dict, list[str]]:
919	    """Verify one range page, returning ``(anchor, tip, verified_tx_ids)``.
920	
921	    Shared core of :func:`verify_range_export` (one page) and
922	    :func:`verify_range_exports` (a batch chaining each page's tip into the
923	    next page's expected anchor). Raises :class:`_Failure` with the public
924	    error category on every defect.
925	    """
926	    anchor = _validate_range_export_inputs(document, expected_anchor, trust)
927	    _authenticate_range_export(document, trust, now)
928	    # The caller-pinned anchor must strictly equal the delivered one.
929	    if document["anchor"] != expected_anchor:
930	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
931	    tail = _recompute_range_tail(anchor, document["blocks"])
932	    tip = _range_tip_descriptor(anchor, tail)
933	    _check_range_tip(document["tip"], tip)
934	    if document["mode"] == "attested":
935	        _verify_range_attestation(document, trust)
936	    verified_ids = sorted(tx.tx_id for block in tail for tx in block.transactions)
937	    return anchor, tip, verified_ids

940	def _validate_range_export_inputs(
941	    document: object, expected_anchor: object, trust: object
942	) -> dict:
943	    """Structural validation of the export document, the pinned anchor and
944	    the trust document. Returns the closed ``{height, block_hash}`` anchor.
945	    """
946	    if not isinstance(document, dict):
947	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
948	    if tuple(document.keys()) != RANGE_EXPORT_KEYS:
949	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
950	    source = document["source"]
951	    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
952	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
953	    request_id = document["request_id"]
954	    if not isinstance(request_id, str) or not request_id:
955	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
956	    if document["mode"] not in RANGE_EXPORT_MODES:
957	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
958	    if not _is_int(document["expires_at"]):
959	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
960	    anchor = _validate_range_anchor(document["anchor"])
961	    # The expected anchor is validated for shape here; the strict equality
962	    # binding itself is an integrity check after authorization and expiry.
963	    _validate_range_anchor(expected_anchor)
964	    blocks = document["blocks"]
965	    if not isinstance(blocks, list) or not blocks:
966	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
967	    tip = document["tip"]
968	    if not isinstance(tip, dict) or set(tip) != _RANGE_TIP_KEYS:
969	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
970	    if document["mode"] == "attested":
971	        attestation = document["attestation"]
972	        if not isinstance(attestation, dict) or set(attestation) != (
973	            _RANGE_ATTESTATION_KEYS
974	        ):
975	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

977	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
978	        version = attestation["version"]
979	        if not _is_int(version) or version < 1:
980	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
981	        if not crypto.is_hex128(attestation["signature"]):
982	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

999	def _validate_range_trust(trust: object) -> None:
1000	    """Structural validation of the trust document's ``sources``/``allowlist``.
1001	
1002	    Mirrors the bundle verifier's trust rules; a ``genesis_hash`` is not
1003	    required here because the caller pins the range anchor directly. The
1004	    optional GET /v1/trust ``source_key_history`` mapping is validated too:
1005	    each source maps to a non-empty ascending array of
1006	    ``{version, public_key, activated_event_id}`` items whose versions are
1007	    dense from 1 with strictly ascending activation ids, both numeric fields
1008	    non-boolean positive integers and the public key 64 lowercase hex.
1009	    """
1010	    if not isinstance(trust, dict):
1011	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1012	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
1013	    if not isinstance(sources, dict):
1014	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1015	    for name, entry in sources.items():
1016	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not isinstance(entry, dict):
1017	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1018	        if not _is_int(entry.get("expires_at")):
1019	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1020	        public_key = entry.get("public_key")
1021	        # Ed25519 public keys are 32 raw bytes, i.e. 64 hex characters.
1022	        if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
1023	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1024	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
1025	    if not isinstance(allowlist, dict):
1026	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1027	    for name, expires_at in allowlist.items():
1028	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not _is_int(expires_at):
1029	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1030	    history = trust.get("source_key_history")
1031	    if history is not None:
1032	        if not isinstance(history, dict):
1033	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1034	        for name, entries in history.items():
1035	            if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
1036	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1037	            if not isinstance(entries, list) or not entries:
1038	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1039	            last_activated = None
1040	            for position, entry in enumerate(entries):
1041	                if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != set(
1042	                    _HISTORY_ENTRY_KEYS
1043	                ):
1044	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1045	                version = entry.get("version")
1046	                public_key = entry.get("public_key")
1047	                activated = entry.get("activated_event_id")
1048	                # Versions are dense from 1; both numeric fields are plain
1049	                # (non-boolean) positive integers.
1050	                if not _is_int(version) or version != position + 1:
1051	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1052	                if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
1053	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1054	                if not _is_int(activated) or activated < 1:
1055	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1056	                if last_activated is not None and activated <= last_activated:
1057	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1058	                last_activated = activated

1066	def _authenticate_range_export(document: dict, trust: dict, now: float) -> None:
1067	    """Check mode-specific source authorization and every deadline.
1068	
1069	    A ``plain`` export is only acceptable from an allowlisted source and must
1070	    carry ``attestation: null``. An ``attested`` export is authorized one of
1071	    two ways:
1072	
1073	    * the trust document carries a ``source_key_history`` mapping (the new
1074	      rule): the source must appear in the mapping — the historical public key
1075	      matching and signature verification happen by attestation version in
1076	      :func:`_verify_range_attestation`; the trust ``sources`` entry and its
1077	      deadline play no role, so a delivery signed under a since-rotated or
1078	      revoked key still authenticates as long as the document itself is
1079	      unexpired;
1080	    * the mapping is absent (the legacy rule): the source must be a
1081	      ``sources`` entry whose unexpired deadline is checked.
1082	
1083	    All deadlines are checked before any integrity work: an expired,
1084	    correctly-signed export is still unusable.
1085	    """
1086	    source = document["source"]
1087	    mode = document["mode"]
1088	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
1089	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
1090	    if mode == "plain":

1115	def _recompute_range_tail(anchor: dict, blocks_raw: list) -> list[Block]:

1117

1119	    ``anchor.height + 1``, the first ``prev_hash`` is the anchor hash and
1120	    later ones link internally, every transaction's tx_id and Ed25519
1121	    signature verifies, tx_ids are unique across the tail and ascending
1122	    inside each block, Merkle roots and block hashes recompute, and a pending
1123	    block may only sit at the tail tip. Every field is checked on the *raw*
1124	    JSON value; type/domain defects (non-integer or negative height,
1125	    non-positive or non-integer amount) are reported as ``input``, while
1126	    recomputation mismatches stay ``integrity``.

1128	    blocks: list[Block] = []
1129	    seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
1130	    for position, block_raw in enumerate(blocks_raw):
1131	        if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
1132	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1133	        height = block_raw.get("height")
1134	        prev_hash = block_raw.get("prev_hash")
1135	        merkle_root = block_raw.get("merkle_root")
1136	        block_hash = block_raw.get("block_hash")
1137	        status = block_raw.get("status")
1138	        txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
1139	        # Same rule as the whole-chain recomputation: a height of the wrong
1140	        # type or sign is a field-type defect (input), never coerced.
1141	        if not _is_int(height) or height < 0:
1142	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1143	        if not isinstance(prev_hash, str):
1144	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1145	        if not crypto.is_hex64(merkle_root) or not crypto.is_hex64(block_hash):
1146	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1147	        if status not in ("pending", "confirmed") or not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
1148	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1149	        if height != anchor["height"] + 1 + position:
1150	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1151	        expected_prev = (
1152	            anchor["block_hash"] if position == 0 else blocks[position - 1].block_hash
1153	        )
1154	        if prev_hash != expected_prev:
1155	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1156	        if position < len(blocks_raw) - 1 and status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
1157	            # A pending block may only sit at the tail tip.
1158	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1159	
1160	        tx_ids: list[str] = []
1161	        for raw_tx in txs_raw:
1162	            if not isinstance(raw_tx, dict):
1163	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1164	            sender = raw_tx.get("from")
1165	            recipient = raw_tx.get("to")
1166	            amount = raw_tx.get("amount")
1167	            signature = raw_tx.get("signature")
1168	            stored_tx_id = raw_tx.get("tx_id")
1169	            if not isinstance(sender, str) or not sender:
1170	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1171	            if not isinstance(recipient, str) or not recipient:
1172	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1173	            # The raw amount must already be a non-boolean positive integer —
1174	            # never a coercible string, float or bool.
1175	            if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
1176	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1177	            if not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature:
1178	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1179	            message = crypto.canonical_message(sender, recipient, amount)
1180	            tx_id = crypto.compute_tx_id(message)
1181	            if stored_tx_id != tx_id or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_tx_id):
1182	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1183	            if not crypto.verify_signature(sender, message, signature):
1184	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

1186	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

1189	        if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
1190	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

1192	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

1223	def _verify_range_attestation(document: dict, trust: dict) -> None:
1224	    """Verify the attested export's Ed25519 signature under the pinned key.
1225	
1226	    Two rules, selected by the trust document:
1227	
1228	    * with ``source_key_history`` present, the attestation's ``version``
1229	      selects the source's historical public key; the source not appearing in
1230	      the mapping, or the attestation version not being one of its dense
1231	      versions, is an authorization failure (``auth``), as is a mismatch
1232	      between the attestation's ``public_key`` and that historical key. The
1233	      Ed25519 signature is then checked over the SHA-256 digest of the
1234	      canonical ``ledger-sync-range-v1`` message — a wrong signature is an
1235	      integrity failure. The attestation's version is already structurally
1236	      guaranteed to be a positive integer.
1237	    * without the mapping (legacy rule), the attestation's ``public_key``
1238	      must be exactly the key the trust document pins in ``sources`` for the
1239	      source (a mismatched credential is an authorization failure) and the
1240	      same signature check follows.
1241	    """
1242	    source = document["source"]
1243	    attestation = document["attestation"]
1244	    if _has_key_history(trust):
1245	        history = trust["source_key_history"].get(source)
1246	        if history is None:
1247	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1248	        version = attestation["version"]
1249	        # Versions are structurally guaranteed dense from 1, so a valid
1250	        # version simply indexes the ascending history.
1251	        if version < 1 or version > len(history):
1252	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1253	        pinned = history[version - 1]["public_key"]
1254	        if attestation["public_key"] != pinned:
1255	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1256	    else:
1257	        pinned = trust.get("sources", {})[source]["public_key"]
1258	        if attestation["public_key"] != pinned:
1259	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1260	    message = attested_range_message(
1261	        source,
1262	        document["request_id"],
1263	        document["expires_at"],
1264	        document["anchor"],
1265	        document["blocks"],
1266	        document["tip"],
1267	    )
1268	    digest = hashlib.sha256(message).digest()
1269	    if not crypto.verify_signature(pinned, digest, attestation["signature"]):
1270	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

1338	def advance(
1339	    path: str,
1340	    docs: object,
1341	    trust: object,
1342	    anchor: object,
1343	    now: object,
1344	) -> dict:
1345	    """Verify a range-export batch and durably checkpoint it at ``path``.
1346	
1347	    ``docs`` is an ordered, non-empty batch of range deliveries verified with
1348	    :func:`verify_range_exports` against ``trust`` and ``anchor`` at time
1349	    ``now``: ``now`` must be a plain (non-boolean) non-negative integer; the
1350	    first use of ``path`` requires a legal ``anchor`` (``{height, block_hash}``),
1351	    while a later advance passes ``None`` (continue from the stored tip) or the
1352	    stored tip's ``{height, block_hash}``.
1353	
1354	    On success the checkpoint is written atomically (a uniquely named temp file
1355	    in the same directory, fsynced and ``os.replace``d under a per-path lock)
1356	    with key order ``generation, anchor, tip, context, state_hash``; generation
1357	    starts at 1 and increments once per successful advance, so a failed
1358	    verification never bumps it. The return value is the verifier result with
1359	    the new ``generation`` appended as the final key.
1360	
1361	    The same transaction appends the new checkpoint to the generation-history
1362	    sidecar at ``path + ".history"`` (see the module docstring for the exact
1363	    format): a missing sidecar is opened at ``base = {0, Z}`` for a first
1364	    advance, or migrated from a pre-existing generation-``g`` checkpoint as
1365	    ``base = {g-1, Z}`` with that checkpoint as the first record; an existing
1366	    sidecar is strictly reloaded and replayed, and its last record must
1367	    reproduce the stored checkpoint. Both files are written under the shared
1368	    per-path lock; an ``io`` failure restores the original bytes of both
1369	    best-effort (crash atomicity across the pair is not guaranteed).
1370	
1371	    Every failure is ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
1372	    ``input`` (bad arguments or checkpoint shape), ``auth``/``expired``/
1373	    ``integrity`` (batch verification), ``state`` (an existing checkpoint or
1374	    sidecar fails its key-order/type/hash/replay checks; it is never truncated
1375	    or rebuilt) and ``io`` (the checkpoint cannot be read or written).
1376	    """
1377	    # Argument shape is validated before any file or verification work.
1378	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
1379	        return _failed_advance(ERR_INPUT)
1380	    if not _is_int(now) or now < 0:
1381	        return _failed_advance(ERR_INPUT)
1382	
1383	    lock = _checkpoint_lock(path)
1384	    with lock:
1385	        try:
1386	            previous = _load_checkpoint(path)
1387	            sidecar = _load_history(_history_path(path))
1388	        except _CheckpointError as failure:
1389	            return _failed_advance(failure.category)
1390	
1391	        if previous is None:
1392	            # A sidecar without its checkpoint is unrecoverable corruption.
1393	            if sidecar is not None:
1394	                return _failed_advance(ERR_STATE)
1395	            # First use: the caller must pin a legal anchor.
1396	            expected_anchor = _validate_advance_anchor(anchor)
1397	            if expected_anchor is None:
1398	                return _failed_advance(ERR_INPUT)
1399	            generation = 0
1400	            base = {"generation": 0, "hash": HISTORY_ZERO_HASH}
1401	            records: list[dict] = []
1402	        else:
1403	            generation = previous["generation"]
1404	            stored_tip = previous["tip"]
1405	            if anchor is None:
1406	                # Continue the continuous chain from the stored closed tip.
1407	                expected_anchor = {
1408	                    "height": stored_tip["height"],
1409	                    "block_hash": stored_tip["tip_hash"],
1410	                }
1411	            else:
1412	                expected_anchor = _validate_advance_anchor(anchor)
1413	                if (
1414	                    expected_anchor is None
1415	                    or expected_anchor
1416	                    != {
1417	                        "height": stored_tip["height"],
1418	                        "block_hash": stored_tip["tip_hash"],
1419	                    }
1420	                ):
1421	                    return _failed_advance(ERR_INPUT)
1422	            if sidecar is None:
1423	                # Migrate a pre-existing checkpoint: it becomes the first
1424	                # record over a zero base one generation below it.
1425	                base = {
1426	                    "generation": generation - 1,
1427	                    "hash": HISTORY_ZERO_HASH,
1428	                }
1429	                records = [_history_record(previous, HISTORY_ZERO_HASH)]
1430	            else:
1431	                # The sidecar's tip record must pin the stored checkpoint.
1432	                if sidecar["records"][-1]["checkpoint"] != previous:
1433	                    return _failed_advance(ERR_STATE)
1434	                base = sidecar["base"]
1435	                records = list(sidecar["records"])
1436	
1437	        result = verify_range_exports(docs, expected_anchor, trust, now)
1438	        if not result.get("ok"):
1439	            return {"ok": False, "error": result["error"]}
1440	
1441	        context = {
1442	            "verified_at": now,
1443	            "trust": trust,
1444	            "documents": docs,
1445	            "verified_tx_ids": result["verified_tx_ids"],
1446	        }
1447	        next_generation = generation + 1
1448	        checkpoint = {
1449	            "generation": next_generation,
1450	            "anchor": result["anchor"],
1451	            "tip": result["tip"],
1452	            "context": context,
1453	        }
1454	        checkpoint["state_hash"] = _checkpoint_state_hash(
1455	            next_generation,
1456	            checkpoint["anchor"],
1457	            checkpoint["tip"],
1458	            checkpoint["context"],
1459	        )
1460	        head = records[-1]["hash"] if records else base["hash"]
1461	        record = _history_record(checkpoint, head)
1462	        history_document = {
1463	            "v": HISTORY_VERSION,
1464	            "base": base,
1465	            "records": records + [record],
1466	            "head": record["hash"],
1467	        }
1468	
1469	        history_path = _history_path(path)
1470	        try:
1471	            original_checkpoint = _read_bytes_or_none(path)
1472	            original_history = _read_bytes_or_none(history_path)
1473	        except OSError:
1474	            return _failed_advance(ERR_IO)
1475	        try:
1476	            _atomic_write_checkpoint(path, checkpoint)
1477	            _atomic_write_history(history_path, history_document)
1478	        except OSError:
1479	            # Compensate: put both files' original bytes back best-effort.
1480	            _restore_bytes(path, original_checkpoint)
1481	            _restore_bytes(history_path, original_history)
1482	            return _failed_advance(ERR_IO)
1483	
1484	        advanced = dict(result)
1485	        advanced["generation"] = next_generation
1486	        return advanced

1513	def _load_checkpoint(path: str) -> dict | None:
1514	    """Strictly load and re-verify an existing advance checkpoint.

1516	    Returns None when no file exists at ``path``. Otherwise validates the exact
1517	    key order and JSON types, recomputes ``state_hash`` over the other fields,
1518	    and replays the stored batch through :func:`verify_range_exports` at the
1519	    context's ``verified_at`` — the batch must chain from the stored anchor to

1521	    ``state`` failure (unreadable JSON is ``io``); the file is never truncated

1529	    except OSError as exc:
1530	        raise _CheckpointError(ERR_IO) from exc

1535	        raise _CheckpointError(ERR_STATE) from exc

1547	    the context's ``verified_at`` — it must chain from the stored anchor to
1548	    the stored tip and reproduce the stored verified tx ids.

1551	        checkpoint["generation"],
1552	        checkpoint["anchor"],
1553	        checkpoint["tip"],
1554	        checkpoint["context"],
1555	    )
1556	    if recomputed != checkpoint["state_hash"]:
1557	        raise _CheckpointError(ERR_STATE)

1562	        checkpoint["anchor"],
1563	        context["trust"],
1564	        context["verified_at"],
1565	    )

1567	        raise _CheckpointError(ERR_STATE)

1569	        raise _CheckpointError(ERR_STATE)
1570	    if replay["tip"] != checkpoint["tip"]:
1571	        raise _CheckpointError(ERR_STATE)
1572	    if replay["verified_tx_ids"] != context["verified_tx_ids"]:
